widgets_values:
.: V2V Editing (replace a character in a target video) --- NOTE: TENDS TO LOOK BETTER ON SINGLE PASS. SEE OPTION ABOVE ---

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the girl whose motion comes from <Video 1> and whose appearance comes from <Picture 1>.
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The girl's appearance is styled from <Picture 1>. Her motion, camera movement, background, and lighting from the video are preserved continuously from start to finish without deviation at any point.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the girl's face, body proportions, and skin tone from <Picture 1> are retained, and her motion, choreography, rhythm, and timing from <Video 1> are retained at every moment. 
<Video 1> (whole-video temporal structure, motion path, camera movement, background, lighting): fully_preserved - the girl's choreography, movement speed, gestures, body positions, camera framing, camera movement, background, and lighting from every frame of <Video 1> are preserved throughout the entire target video without deviation.

detailed_description:
The target video uses a naturalistic style matching the source footage, preserving its original lighting, color grading, and camera work.
[Shot 1] The camera follows <Subject 1>, the girl, as she exists in the same setting from <Video 1>. Her appearance matches <Picture 1> — same skin tone, body shape, and natural contours. Throughout the entire video, her motion is a frame-by-frame motion match to <Video 1>: the same choreography, gestures, limb positions, movement speed, and rhythm are followed continuously from start to finish. The camera framing, angle, and movement stay locked to <Video 1> at all times. The background remains identical and unchanged.


.: Reference Generation (general filmmaking):

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the character in <Picture 1>. (basic description)

<Subject 2> is the scene location in <Picture 2>. (basic scene description)

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] highly realistic live-action scene of <Subject 1> in <Subject 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre guides the vocal delivery of <Subject 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1]: a close up shot of <Subject 1> with a shocked expression as the camera pulls in towards her face. Suddenly, she turns around to look behind her.
[Shot 2]: a 3/4ths shot of <Subject 1> as she turns, her expression is confused. She tilts her head to one side, a look of questioning. She hesitantly says using <Audio 1> as her vocal-timbre reference: <d>[English]Hello?.. Is anyone there?</d> her tone is hesitant and suspicious.
[Shot 3]: an over-the-shoulder following shot as <Subject 1> begins to walk through <Subject 2> looking around side to side.
 
overall_soundscape:
interior ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

# MiniMax H3 Workflow Refactor

> **Design philosophy:** The user should control meaningful settings, while the workflow handles the internal routing, dependencies, and consequences automatically.

---

## Instructions

### 1. Prepare the Load Nodes

Disable any load nodes you're not using. Load media into every node you are using.

### 2. Configure the Control Panel

Use the **Control Panel** for the main workflow settings.

Set:

- Resolution
- Duration
- Reference counts
- Reference toggles
- Video Continuation
- Force Audio
- Final Upscale
- Interpolation
- Sparse Attention / VRAM options
- Sampler-related options

The workflow will handle the internal routing automatically based on those controls.

### 3. Configure References

Enable the references you want to use from the **Control Panel**.

You do not need to manually bypass individual reference groups.

Load the media you want to use into the corresponding:

- `<Picture>` reference nodes
- `<Audio>` reference nodes
- `<Video>` reference nodes

Only the references enabled by the controls are used for generation.

### 4. Set Video Reference Resolution Limits

When using a **video reference**, set the **Width** and **Height** values in the corresponding **Load Video** node to the maximum dimensions you want the reference video to use.

For example:

```text
Width: 768
Height: 768
Maintain Aspect Ratio: Selected

## Masking Options

### 1. Choose a Masking Tool

Use the **masking selector** to choose **SAM**, **Manual Mask Upload**, or **Animated Mask Drawer**.

Set **Crop Sampling to Mask** to `true` if you want MVEx to crop around the masked area during sampling.

**Base_Video** saves the selected video to your ComfyUI `temp` folder. You can use it with a third-party masking tool, then load the resulting mask through **Manual Mask Upload**.

### 2. SAM

Enter a text prompt describing what you want to mask. If SAM detects multiple objects, set the **object index** and use **Track Preview** to check that it follows the correct object.

### 3. Manual Mask Upload

Drag and drop your mask video into **Manual Mask Upload**. Enable **Fill Holes** to close unwanted gaps inside the masked area. Leave it off if those gaps are intentional.

### 4. Animated Mask Drawer

1. Queue the workflow once to load video frames into the drawer.
2. Click **Launch Mask Editor** and draw a rectangle, circle, or Bézier shape over the area you want to mask.
3. Move through the timeline. Reposition or resize the shape on frames where the subject moves; the drawer creates keyframes and fills in the motion between them.
4. Click **Save & Return to ComfyUI**, then queue the workflow again to generate the mask.

### 5. Check **Mask_Preview** node and adjust as needed.

[Animated Mask Drawer instructions](https://comfy.icu/node/AnimatedMaskDrawer)

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the adult woman whose complete appearance comes from <Picture 1>.
<Picture 1> is the image reference for <Subject 1>, including her face, body proportions, skin tone, pink wavy hair and bangs, makeup, glossy red clown nose, rainbow-striped choker, bright-pink costume, white shoulder decorations, and pink gloves.
<Video 1> is the source video being edited. It guides the shot duration, camera movement, framing, and timing of <Subject 1>'s movements.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 1> watching the woman positioned in the center of the frame as that woman speaks. <Subject 1> maintains an annoyed expression. At exactly 00:07.000, <Subject 1> rolls her eyes, looks away, and crosses her arms. Her appearance remains consistent with <Picture 1> throughout.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve the recognizable appearance established by <Picture 1> across every frame, including her face, hair, makeup, costume, accessories, and changing facial expressions.
<Video 1> (source edit for [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - retain its duration, camera movement, framing, setting, and action timing. Adapt the composition as needed to position <Subject 1> naturally beside the woman speaking in the center of the frame.

detailed_description:
The video has a polished live-action style with natural lighting, realistic skin and fabric textures, and fluid camera movement. A woman positioned in the center of the frame speaks while <Subject 1> stands beside her and watches.

[Shot 1] In one continuous live-action shot, <Subject 1> watches the woman in the center of the frame as the woman speaks. <Subject 1> looks visibly annoyed, maintaining a tense expression with subtly tightened lips and an impatient gaze.

At exactly 00:07.000, <Subject 1> reacts to the speaking woman by rolling her eyes upward. She then turns her face and gaze away from the woman while bringing both arms across her torso into a clearly crossed-arm posture. After crossing her arms, she continues looking away with an irritated, dismissive expression.

Keep the reaction natural and clearly readable. Preserve believable posture, eye movement, facial animation, and timing. Keep <Subject 1>'s pink wavy hair and bangs, makeup, glossy red clown nose, rainbow-striped choker, bright-pink costume, white shoulder decorations, and pink gloves consistent throughout.

overall_soundscape:
N/A - no audio instructions.

N/A - no music instructions.
